## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Saṁghabheda Sutta* is the eighth discourse of the fifth chapter (*Soṇavagga*) of the *Udāna* in the Khuddaka Nikāya, referenced at page 60 of the Pali Text Society edition [SuttaCentral]. The narrative relates to the impending schism within the monastic community, recording the episode where Devadatta declares his intention to cause a split in the Sangha [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral connect the text to verse collections across different Buddhist traditions, including chapter 28 (*Pāpavarga*) of the Sanskrit *Udānavarga*, its Tibetan translation, and its Chinese translations (*Chufa yaoji jing*, T 212.29, and *Faji yao song jing*, T 213.28) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also identifies a canonical narrative parallel in the *Saṁghabhedakakkhandhaka* (Kd 17) of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral].
This Vinaya parallel is corroborated by DharmaNexus, which detects extensive Pali-internal text reuse between segments 1.3–6.4 of the sutta and Kd 17 (§§3.17.1–3.17.16), sharing roughly 1,791 characters [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records substantial overlap with the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* (§§4.1–6.4), as well as shared formulaic phrases across various Nikāya discourses (including AN 7, SN 12, MN 86, and DN 16) and a cross-language alignment with the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu* [DharmaNexus]. None of the examined secondary literature passages treat this specific *Udāna* discourse directly, referring instead to the general institutional concept of schism or to Vinaya narrative works.
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
